leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part prize on B028 (GLP-1). Five members (El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) name Drucker, Holst and Mojsov with a citation centred on GLP-1 physiology and its active form. Linnarsson names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation that includes development into therapies. The shared elements are the first-place ranking, the three-name limit, and the view that the discovery chain is complete and mature. Not shared is the third laureate and therefore whether the citation rewards physiology and peptide identification or also the drug-development step. Habener is outside the credited names, and several members record that this leaves any trio open to challenge. Four members (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius) say they would consider Knudsen if the committee prefers a therapy-oriented citation, and Sandberg would put Knudsen first among those he would reconsider. Linnarsson in turn describes the physiology-only trio as the main competing configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All six members rank and prefer B028 as the single prize part, and each states the merits independently of the unanimous opening ranking: a complete arc from proglucagon processing and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide through incretin physiology to drugs with confirmed benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal outcomes.
No member considers maturity or timing a weakness for B028; the mechanism is described as stable and the clinical effect as still growing.

All six identify attribution as the main weakness of B028: Habener is not among the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is described as contested, and the three-name limit forces an exclusion.
Members agree that the supplied text cannot settle the priority history. Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson state that their recollection of it is unverified.
Optogenetics (B014) is not preferred by any member. Members who discuss it (El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg) say six credited names cannot be reduced to three without excluding someone decisive.
No member proposes a two-part prize in the round-1 configurations. Several say the three-name limit is already used by B028.
scientific_disputes: Whether B028 should be framed as a prize for hormone physiology and peptide identification, or for the arc from physiology to long-acting therapy. Five members frame it as discovery; Linnarsson argues that converting native GLP-1 into a once-weekly agent needed new insight (albumin binding, DPP-4 resistance) and was not routine engineering.

Whether a prize that rewards a drug class with a large commercial footprint can be read as rewarding discovery rather than commercial success (raised by El Manira and Linnarsson), and whether long-term safety and durability after discontinuation are adequately settled (El Manira, Sandberg).

Which second candidate, if any, follows B028. B045 (CAR-T) is a named alternative for Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson. B020 (unfolded protein response) is an alternative for El Manira, Sandberg and Svenningsson, and is called a clean basic-science option by Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius. B014 (optogenetics) is an alternative for El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius.
How narrowly a B020 citation should be worded. Svenningsson notes the PERK, ATF6 and integrated stress response arms and says the citation would need to focus on the IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1 mechanism.
Whether optogenetics is a method that opens a field, which Perlmann says the prize has honoured, or a research tool with modest medical impact, as El Manira, Sandberg and Linnarsson describe it.
attribution_disputes: B028 third seat: Mojsov (El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) versus Knudsen (Linnarsson). Linnarsson also notes that adding Mojsov imports a priority dispute with the Habener group, while Wahren-Herlenius says her identification and synthesis of the peptide is documented well enough to justify credit and that excluding her risks a mistake the field would remember.
Habener's role in proglucagon and GLP-1 biology is raised by all six members, but he is not in the credited list and no configuration includes him. It is not resolved how this should be handled.

B045 (CAR-T): the credited trio is June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, and the members who discuss it (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg) say Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a separate lineage from the costimulated chimeric receptor. They treat June and Sadelain as the cleaner pair. Eshhar, who originated the chimeric receptor, is not credited.

B014 (optogenetics): six credited names for at most three seats, with priority contested between channel discovery (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann) and neuronal application (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenbock).

B020 (Walter and Mori) has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist according to El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius. B051 (cGAS-STING) is described as cleanest with Chen and Barber, but Sandberg notes that cyclic-dinucleotide work by Vance, Patel and others and near-simultaneous discovery complicate it. B019 (HPV VLP) is complicated by the NIH versus Queensland priority question and the late Jian Zhou (Svenningsson).

Whether an industry-based scientist can be a laureate. Sandberg says neither the rule nor precedent excludes this and the question is the nature of the contribution. Wahren-Herlenius says it changes the character of the prize.
maturity_disputes: B020 (UPR): El Manira, Perlmann and Svenningsson cite decades of confirmation. Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius say therapeutic translation is thin or indirect, and Wahren-Herlenius would back it as a later prize or an alternative.

B045 (CAR-T): Wahren-Herlenius cites durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancy as a stronger maturity case than B020 or B014. El Manira prefers to hold it for a year when the committee agrees on what the achievement is.

B051 (cGAS-STING): Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius say clinical translation is unproven because modulators are still in trials. Wahren-Herlenius says the interferonopathy genetics are narrower in impact than incretin therapy.

B037 (antisense for SMN2) is ranked third by Sandberg for dramatic clinical effect and compact credit. Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius rank it lower, citing narrower support and a still-accumulating proof of concept for the modality. Perlmann also notes that the credited names omit early SMN2 oligonucleotide work.
B019 (HPV VLP) is described by Svenningsson as a later-year candidate because of the earlier HPV and cervical cancer prize and the unresolved VLP priority dispute.

B041 (BCR-ABL inhibition) has exceptional clinical impact (Linnarsson), but Svenningsson says the credited trio sits downstream of Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion work that is not credited.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy); neither is credited on any shortlisted candidate, and he reports no recusal issue.

El Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner; neither is a candidate. He notes a topical interest in optogenetics as a method, not a personal or institutional connection.

Perlmann discloses co-authorship with Svenningsson and El Manira, described as collegial and not a recusal issue, and prior nuclear receptor work with Ronald Evans that does not overlap with the shortlist.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation with other members; none involves a shortlisted candidate.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that B051 (cGAS-STING) and B045 (CAR-T) touch immunology adjacent to her field, with no documented tie to any credited name. Linnarsson notes optogenetics is adjacent to his field and reports no documented involvement.
No member reports a conflict requiring recusal on any shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: Should the B028 citation reward only the physiology and identification of GLP-1 and its active form, or also the development of long-acting therapies? The laureate set and the citation wording depend on this.

Does the supplied record support Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide well enough to place her in the third seat, and if it does not, is Knudsen the preferred third name or should the seat be left to a different rationale?
How should the committee deal with Habener's absence from the credited names, given that all six members flag it? Does it affect which trio is defensible, or must it be stated in the citation?
If Drucker, Holst and Mojsov holds four or more votes, what is the position of the Knudsen-preferring minority, and what threshold of support would make each side reopen the allocation?

Should a second prize part be added to B028 at all, given the three-name limit? If so, which of B020, B045 or B014 would members support, and with which exact names (for example Walter and Mori for B020, or June and Sadelain for B045)?
For B045, is Rosenberg's inclusion defensible as part of the same achievement, or should the citation be limited to the chimeric receptor lineage, and how should Eshhar's omission be treated?
Can any configuration of B014 be defended within three names, or should it be set aside for this year on credit grounds alone?
Is there a case for placing B020 ahead of B045 if therapeutic maturity is weighted less than conceptual clarity of attribution, and how would members state that weighting?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show full agreement that B028 should be the single prize part, and the only live question inside it is the third name (Mojsov in five configurations, Knudsen in one) and with it whether the citation honours discovery or development. Members state that the supplied text cannot settle Mojsov's priority and that Habener's omission affects every trio. Four members say they would accept Knudsen if a majority prefers a therapy-oriented citation, and Linnarsson says he would not treat the choice as a point of principle, so the disagreement appears narrower than the stated positions suggest. For a second candidate, the members' alternatives are split across B045, B020 and B014, with attribution concerns attached to each. No member has proposed a two-part configuration, and no conflict requiring recusal has been disclosed.
